title: Magnetic-Free Quantum Interference and Universal Josephson Diode Effect Driven by a Supercurrent Gauge Field
authors: Haowei Ye, Wenxue He, Kaixuan Fan, Yingpeng Zhang, Shijin Li, Yu Pan, Dechao Geng, Fan Yang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Hechen Ren
abstract: The Josephson effect, a hallmark of superconducting phase coherence, drives modern quantum technologies. However, Josephson-based quantum interference has hitherto been tethered to magnetic fields, despite phase coherence being a quintessential, intrinsic trait of superconductivity. Moreover, the Josephson diode effect (JDE) is typically viewed as an anomalous phenomenon indicative of broken symmetries in exotic phases of matter. Here, in planar Josephson junctions made with $\mathrm{Bi}_2\mathrm{O}_2\mathrm{Se}$ and bilayer graphene, we demonstrate that the JDE is a missing universal property of the Josephson effect. Simultaneously, we present an all-electric technology that replaces magnetic flux for controlling and measuring supercurrent interference. Central to our approach is a supercurrent gauge field (SGF), generated and amplified through high-kinetic-inductance superconductors and novel device architectures. By establishing the physical equivalence between the SGF and a magnetic field, we eliminate the reliance on external fields in quantum interference and reveal a universal, field-free JDE mechanism with broad implications for detecting broken-symmetry states. Finally, we show that the SGF offers capabilities beyond those of a conventional magnetic field by experimentally demonstrating a magnetic-free, phase-sensitive technique to construct and characterize finite-momentum superconductivity, opening new frontiers for exploring novel phases of matter and superconducting quantum architectures.
summary: This paper introduces the concept of a Supercurrent Gauge Field (SGF) that allows for the generation of magnetic-field-like effects in Josephson junctions using only electric currents. By demonstrating this, the authors show that both quantum interference and the Josephson Diode Effect can be controlled entirely electrically, opening pathways for compact superconducting quantum devices.
main_problem: The research aims to eliminate the historical dependence of Josephson quantum interference and the Josephson Diode Effect (JDE) on external magnetic fields.
main_result: They demonstrate that a supercurrent gauge field (SGF), generated purely by electric currents, can induce both macroscopic quantum interference patterns and the JDE, establishing an all-electric control mechanism.
method: The study combines theoretical modeling based on Ginzburg-Landau theory with detailed transport measurements in planar Josephson junctions using varying current configurations.
model_or_system: The physical platform consists of planar Josephson junctions made from materials like Bi2O2Se and bilayer graphene. The physics is modeled by treating the supercurrent gauge field (SGF) as an effective replacement for the magnetic vector potential A in the superconducting order parameter phase gradient.
key_observables: Supercurrent Interference Patterns (SIPs), Josephson Diode Effect (JDE) asymmetry ($I_{	ext{C}}^+$ vs $I_{	ext{C}}^-$), and Negative Differential Resistance (NDR).
important_parameters: Bias current, control currents ($I_1, I_2$), external magnetic fields ($B_x, B_y$), and temperature.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the physical equivalence between the SGF generated by supercurrents and an externally applied magnetic field. It also models the system using Ginzburg-Landau theory approximations for current density.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the emergence of JDE in asymmetric current configurations (field-free), show how control currents can modulate interference patterns mimicking flux sweeping, and detail the dependence of JDE on external fields and temperature.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the problem (B-field reliance), then introducing the SGF concept via theoretical modeling (Ginzburg-Landau/gauge invariance), demonstrating its realization through current injection in asymmetric junctions to show field-free interference, and finally confirming the universal nature of JDE using this electric control.
why_interesting: The work provides a powerful analogy between magnetic flux quantization and supercurrent phase winding, offering an all-electric means to probe fundamental superconducting phenomena like momentum transfer and diode behavior without external magnets. This is highly relevant for developing compact quantum devices.
